page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m4.large is an entry-tier virtual machine belonging to the Shared instance family. Running on a KVM hypervisor, it is configured with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The compute allocation provides 2 burstable vCPUs originating from 1 physical core across 2 hardware threads. The system includes 8.0 GB of memory, delivering 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance comes without bundled local storage, includes no GPU accelerators, and operates with a 0 Gbps baseline network bandwidth specification.

Benchmark results highlight baseline entry-level performance typical of shared and burstable CPU configurations. The system registered 1161.28 on the single-core stress-ng benchmark and 2371.48 under multi-core stress testing. Geekbench evaluations returned scores of 1092.0 for single-core and 1822.0 for multi-core processing, alongside a PassMark CPU metric of 3062.61. Memory bandwidth tests reached 22.38 GB/sec for uncached 256MB reads and 19.14 GB/sec for uncached writes, reflecting lower-tier memory throughput compared to dedicated instances.

The burstable CPU model offers cost efficiency for workloads with intermittent execution profiles, minimizing infrastructure expense when full continuous core capacity is unnecessary. The absence of local disk storage and baseline network limits require external network-attached volumes and modest network demands. Appropriate workloads for ecs.t6-c1m4.large include low-traffic web applications, development and testing environments, staging systems, and intermittent background microservices.
